correctness.rationale: The identity g_i+g_j=(x_i+x_j)(T+x_i+x_j) gives at most two distinct coordinate values at a field-valued critical point. For n divisible by four, counting parity in a gradient evaluation forces the nonzero point to be an indicator vector supported on 1 mod 4 indices. There are n-1 independent-in-height homogeneous gradient quadrics, so the ideal is a saturated complete intersection of degree 2^(n-1). Each displayed Q_S contains the gradient ideal, is line-primary with ring k[u,v]/(v^2), and contributes projective length two. The 2^(n-2) components have the same total degree as the gradient scheme, forcing equality of saturated ideals. The finite script verifies GF(2) support and graded Hilbert calculations at n=4,8, and local conditions up to n=16; the proof, not those tests, covers every positive multiple of four.

value.rationale: The full scheme structure is a natural unresolved refinement of the derivative-locus dimension problem: every nonzero component, length-two local primary ring, saturation, absence of embedded points and exact Hilbert series are determined for all n=4m. The unbounded exponential number of non-coordinate components for n>=8 makes the scheme classification substantive, beyond calculating a few cases or an elementary numerical consequence.
